characters.name: Peter Parker / Spider-Man
characters.description: You've heard the story a dozen times in a dozen different ways. Peter Benjamin Parkeris anawkward andintrovertedscience nerdand high-school studentwho was bitten by a genetically augmented spider during a tour of the ESU labs. Imbued with the ability to do most of "whatever a spider can," and giving himself the artificial ability to spin webs with wrist-mounted web-shooters and synthetic web-fluid of his unique creation, Peter decided togratify his hungry and malnourished egoby getting into wrestling and TV showbiz as The Amazing Spider-Man. Blinded by his self-centered desires, Peterrefused to helpa security guard nab a burglar who robbed the fight promoter's office. It was as a consequence of this that the burglarlater shot and killed Peter's uncle and surrogate father Ben Parkerafter breaking into the Parker family's suburban home in Forest Hills. Distraught at his uncle's death, Peter pursed the killer to a warehouse and struck him down, seeking his revenge. It was only after unmasking the killer and recognizing him as the burglar that he could have stopped,but didn't, that Peter finally understood the meaning of Uncle Ben's moralistic adage:"With great power, there must also come great responsibility."Ever since then, Peter has been fighting urban crime and corruption and saving lives in New York Cityas Spider-Manin order to atone for his past sins. Action Hero: Spider-Man has experienced a great deal of action throughout his superhero career. Adaptational Angst Downgrade: In the comics, Peter didn't meet any of his usual friends until college and spent most of his time in high-school alone and unwanted, contributing to his bitterness. Having grown up with people like Gwen and Eddie, as well as having a small social group of friends at Midtown in the show, Peter is much happier as a result. As a matter of fact, he starts out the series actually beingexcitedto go back to school following summer break, if only because heeagerly assumes having powers will make thi

characters.name: Gwen Stacy
characters.description: Gwendolyn Stacy is friends with Peter Parker and Harry Osborn. She is the daughter of New York City Police Department captain George Stacy. Despite romantic feelings between her and Peter, she dated Harry when Peter began dating Liz Allan. Adaptational Early Appearance: Much like inUltimate Spider-Man (2000), Gwen knows Peter in high school instead of meeting him in college. Adaptational Intelligence: While Gwen was never lacking in intellect, in the comics andDepending on the Writer, she has been portrayed as having somewhat of an interest in science, but wasn't as academically-inclined and overtly nerdy as this interpretation of Gwen is. Adaptation Personality Change: In the comics, Gwen was a popular beauty queen from high school who was introduced as anAlpha Bitchbefore having her personalitysoftenedinto more of a teary-eyed and emotional character who tends to constantly worry about Peter. In the show, she is every bit as unpopular and nerdy as Peter and is a lot less patient toward his constant disappearances and inability to communicate with her. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: In the original comics, Gwen met Peter in college and was initially icy towards him before her shift in personality led to them becoming anOfficial Couple. Here, she admits to having loved him sinceseventh gradeand is already one of his closest friends in high school by the start of the series. She also never develops a dislike for Spider-Man like in the comics.

characters.name: Harry Osborn
characters.description: Harry Osborn is the son of industry magnate Norman Osborn and the best friend of Peter Parker. Like many versions, he struggles with his resentment toward his best friend along with his desperation to get his father's attention. Abusive Parents: His father is extremely neglectful as well as outright verbally and emotionally abusive towards him, regularly crapping on Harry's self-esteem while showingblatant favoritismtowards Peter and only ever spending proper time with Harry tocultivate his negative qualities. Not to mention, his mother hardly even speaks to him, implying that they don't have much of a relationship at all. It's no wonder Harry has so many issues. Acquired Situational Narcissism: When he succeeds in getting popular for a time after making the football team and dosing on the Goblin drug, he's not too shy aboutgetting ahead with the in-crowd, and he snubs his former friends Peter and Gwen at social functions. Adaptational Early Appearance:Much likeUltimate Spider-Man (2000), Harry knows Peter in high school instead of meeting him in college.AZig-Zaggedexample comes into play in regard to the Green Goblin identity. Harry seemingly turns out to be Gobby in "The Uncertainty Principal", thus meaning he predates his father in the role in this continuity… until it's later revealed that itwasNorman the entire time and he simply framed and gaslit his own son. That said, Harry begins using the Goblin serum and gains the strength and manic tendencies of the Green Goblin while his father is still alive, rather than that being a development that occurs after his father's demise. Much likeUltimate Spider-Man (2000), Harry knows Peter in high school instead of meeting him in college.

characters.name: Mary Jane Watson
characters.description: Mary Jane Watson, or simply MJ, is a beautiful girl who is the niece of Anna Watson. Aborted Arc: She and Peter were meant to be the series' endgameOfficial Couple, but the cancellation kept this from playing out. Adaptational Early Appearance: While not to the same degree asUltimate Spider-Man (2000), MJ knows Peter in high school instead of meeting him in college.noteIn theUltimatecomics, MJ was around before Gwen; here, it's the other way around. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul:Unlike the comics, where she briefly dated Harry but eventually broke up with him due to his clinginess and neuroticism, here the two rarely interact with each other.She also briefly shows an interest in Mark Allan (the show's incarnation of Mark Raxton from the comics), while their comic book counterparts had no romantic tension whatsoever. Unlike the comics, where she briefly dated Harry but eventually broke up with him due to his clinginess and neuroticism, here the two rarely interact with each other.

characters.name: Flash Thompson
characters.description: Eugene Thompson, better known by the nickname Flash, is a high school student and star football player. While coming off as a typical jock and bully, he gradually grows into a better person. Adaptational Angst Downgrade: Flash in the comics comes from a broken home with anAbusive Dad. Here, that's implied not to be the case, as his father when briefly shown appears genuinely concerned about his son when Flash is in the hospital, and his mother doesn't make any references to her husband mistreating him. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: His mom manages to be this, inadvertently humiliating him at his birthday party by inviting Peter and revealing they were once friends. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: Despite bullying Peter, there are moments in the series where Flash's childhood friendship with him shines through. Notably, Flash trusts Peter enough to prevent him from saying something dumb while on a date for Valentines Day and Peter sincerely thanks him for calling him out on his behavior while wearing the symbiote.Peter:Thanks for the reality check.Flash:[smiling]Don't mention it. Book Dumb: He is notcompletelystupid (especially compared to his pal,Kenny Kong), but still a walking academic disaster area.

characters.name: Liz Allan
characters.description: Liz Allan is a popular girl and cheerleader at Midtown High. Initially dismissive of geeky Peter Parker, she grows more fond of him as their social circles become intertwined. This grows into full-blown romantic attraction and she becomes Peter's first girlfriend. Adaptational Dye-Job: Is brunette here rather than blonde, befitting herRace Lift. Adaptational Relationship Overhaul: While her comic incarnation had feelings for Peter in high school, it never went anywhere with Peter beinguninterested. Here, they actually date. Affectionate Nickname: Once she takes a shine to Peter, she calls him "Petey." All Guys Want Cheerleaders: She's one of the school cheerleaders, which is why she's so popular at school.

characters.name: J. Jonah Jameson
characters.description: J. Jonah Jameson is the publisher ofThe Daily Buglenewspaper and the father of astronaut John Jameson. He is known for his hatred of Spider-Man. Alliterative Name:JohnJonahJameson. Benevolent Boss: It's hidden underneath hisMean Bossexterior, but Jonahdoeslegitimately care about his staff and even keeps Peter safe from The Rhino. Catchphrase: Saying he wants to do something/that he wants something done, and then expressing the unreasonable amount of time it should be done in seconds, often with a decimal and additional threat. (Example: "I want a title in 7.3 seconds or you're all fired!") Disproportionate Retribution: While Jameson hated Spider-Man from the very beginning of the series, it was when he finds out a rival paper's story on Spidey outsold theBugle's story on his son's return from space that causes him to decide to run a smear campaign against Spidey, outraged that Spider-Man gained more attention than his son.

characters.name: George Stacy
characters.description: George Stacy is a captain in the New York Police Department and the father of Gwen Stacy. Adaptational Early Appearance: While not to the same degree asUltimate Spider-Man (2000), Captain Stacy knows Peter in high school instead of meeting him in college.noteHis Ultimate counterpart actually predates his daughter's debut and is one of the officers going after Uncle Ben's killer. Age Lift: He's nowhere as old as 616 George Stacy, who was white haired and retired from the NYPD. Ascended Extra: He is a minor character in the first season but becomes a close ally of Spider-Man throughout the second season. Badass Normal: He's got no powers whatsoever, but he's the Captain of the NYPD for a good reason.

characters.name: May Parker
characters.description: May Parker is the widow of the deceased Ben Parker and aunt to the orphan Peter Parker. Adaptational Attractiveness: Just like her Ultimate counterpart, May is significantly more younger-looking than her traditionally wizened portrayal in the mainstream comics. Adaptational Personality Change: In the comics, she's usually depicted as having an open dislike for Spider-Man. Here, much like theSam Raimi film trilogy, she seems to view him as a hero and even stands up for him in front of Doctor Octopus. Almighty Mom: Or Almighty Aunt, in this case, but she's willing to stand up for her nephew when necessary. Composite Character: Of herself. She is nigh-identical to her mainstream comic book counterpart, but has a slightly more youthful appearance like her counterpart in theUltimate Spider-Man (2000)comics and retains herRaimi filmcounterpart's trait of lacking any dislike towards Spider-Man.

characters.name: Ben Parker
characters.description: Peter Parker's uncle, who raised him along with May Parker in their Forest Hills home after his parents died in a plane crash. While he was tragically shot and killed by a burglar, his wise words and sage advice are the driving force behind Peter's heroism. Cool Uncle: Overlapping withCool Old Guy, but he is shown to have been a fairly close and laid backParental Substituteto Peter. Death by Origin Story: His murder set Peter down the path of using his powers for good. Happily Married: To Aunt May, until his death. Maybe Magic, Maybe Mundane: Was the Uncle Ben who helped Peter in "Intervention" just a memory, a representation of his conscience, or was it actually Uncle Ben in some otherworldly form? The fact that he was able to interact with Peter and the symbiote suggests he was a bit more complex than just something Peter imagined.

characters.name: Richard & Mary Parker
characters.description: Adaptation Distillation: Richard's stated backstory of being the partner of Eddie's father borrows heavily from his Ultimate counterpart, though his connections to the symbiote are not present here. The Ghost: Aside from ablink-and-you'll miss it photo, they do not appear once even in flashbacks. Posthumous Character: They are long deceased by the start of the series. Unnamed Parent: Neither are explicitly named, but going off most adaptations and the comics, they are likely Richard and Mary.

characters.name: Randy "Rand" Robertson
characters.description: Rand Robertson is on the Midtown High School football team with Flash Thompson, but is shown in the show to be much nicer and more neutral than his teammates. He is dating Sally Avril and is Robbie Robertson's son. Adaptational Early Appearance: This version of Randy knows Peter in high school instead of meeting him later on in life. Adaptation Personality Change: Randy in the comics is a hotheaded activist who is unafraid to speak his mind. Rand here is a laidbackNice Guywho tries to avoid as much conflict as possible. Alliterative Name:RandyRobertson. Big Eater: He is one according to his father.

characters.name: Sally Avril
characters.description: Rand Robertson's snobby cheerleader girlfriend. Adaptation Dye-Job: This version of Sally Avril is a blonde. She had black hair in the comics,though she did wear a blonde wig as Bluebird. Adaptational Nice Girl:Downplayed, but a significant yet subtle change is that this version of Sally Avril is slightly kinder than her comic counterpart. Both versions of Sally arecruel, popular girlswho only care about their shallow view of high school popularityand look down on those they deem beneath them, like Peter Parker. However, Sally in the showhas limits to her meanness. The comics version of Sally isunapologetically cruel, showingNo Sympathywhen Peter's uncle Ben diesandeven coaxing Liz Allan away from showing any remorse. In contrast, this Sally, though still a jerk, hasmoments of genuine concern: she expresses worry when Peter's aunt May is in the hospital, tries to hold back from mocking him, and shows alarm when his life is in danger. Thesesmall acts of compassion, despite her dislike of Peter, reveal that the show's Sally has a moral boundary her comic original lacks. All Guys Want Cheerleaders: In the first episode, Peter has a big crush on her and asks her out. The results? They ain't pretty. Alpha Bitch: She fits this archetype even more than Liz, who at least undergoesCharacter Development; Sally simply remains an abrasive, judgmentalJerkassfor most of the show's run, and is ridiculously obsessed with how she and her social clique are perceived by the students at Midtown High.

characters.name: Kenny Kong
characters.description: Flash and Rand's friend and teammate on the Midtown High School football team, who is in a relationship with Glory Grant. He often joins Flash in picking on Peter. Adaptational Dumbass: In the comics, he wassmarter than he appearedand was even able to deduce that Peter was Spider-Man completely on his own. This version of Kong is shown to be more simple-minded. Adaptational Jerkass: The original version of Kenny in theUltimate Spider-Man (2000)comics was essentially that universe's equivalent to the mainstream Flash Thompsonnotewhile the actual Flash was present, he was alotmore irredeemable and the positive traits of his mainsrream portrayal weregivento Kongin that while initially a buffoonish bully, he eventuallybecame much nicer over time. Here, he doesn't undergo much development and remains a simple-minded, immatureJerk Jockfor most of the show. Adaptation Name Change: His last name in the comics wasMcFarlane, with "Kong" being a nickname. Here, Kong has been made hisactuallast name to complement theRace Lift. Alliterative Name:KennyKong.

characters.name: Glory Grant
characters.description: Glory Grant is a student at Midtown High School who is dating Kenny Kong. She's part of Flash's group of friends, though she seems to be more arts-oriented than the others. Adaptational Early Appearance: In relation to herAge Lift, she knows Peter Parker in high school, rather than meeting him after college as in the comics. Age Lift: Glory was in her mid-20s in the comics and previous adaptations. In this adaptation, she is a teenager. Alliterative Name:GloryGrant. Closer to Earth: She is this compared to any of the other popular girls. She's the only one who'snotinstinctively jealous of MJ at first. This is also present in her relationship with Kenny.

characters.name: Sha Shan Nguyen
characters.description: Sha Shan Nguyen is a student at Midtown High who is Flash Thompson's love interest after being dumped by Liz Allan in the show. Adaptational Early Appearance: This version of Sha Shan is a part of Peter's life in high school instead of meeting him in college. Adaptational Heroism: In the original comics, Sha Shan started off as a Spider-Man villain named Sister Sun. InSpectacular, she's a normal high school student and Flash Thompson'sReplacement Goldfishfor Liz Allan. Adaptational Wimp: There's no indication she has her comics-counterpart's martial arts training or ability to shoot an energy beam when holding Brother Power's hand (although the later is admittedly because Brother Powernever appearsin any form during the show's run). Asian and Nerdy: She's smarter than most girls around, much to Flash's chagrin:Flash:She's, like, totally immune to The Flash!Peter:'Cause she's got a brain?Flash:Exactly!

characters.name: Hobie Brown
characters.description: A student at Midtown and member of the football team. He's the subject of aRunning Gagwhere he's interrupted before he can say anything. Adaptational Heroism: He shows no signs of becoming Prowler like in the comics. Adaptational Wimp: While his comic book counterpart became The Prowler, a tech-enhanced thief and ally to Spider-Man, here he remains a non-powered member of the show's supporting cast. Always Second Best: He can't hold a candle to Harry or Peter at the football tryouts and loses out to Harry in bagging the lead role in the play.Though when Harry misses out, he proves to be an excellent replacement. Butt-Monkey: Poor guy keeps getting interrupted.

characters.name: Seymour O'Reilly
characters.description: An extremely energetic student who commentates the school's football matches. Adaptational Nice Guy: In the comics, he was nothing but an immature bully who sucked up to popular kids like Flash Thompson while bullying and making fun of unpopular kids like Peter Parker. In this cartoon, Seymour is a much more kind and likable person who, while not part of the popular crowd, gets along with almosteveryone, from the jocks to the nerds, in contrast to his arrogant and unlikable comic counterpart. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul:In the comics, he's part of Flash Thompson’s gang and a popular student who sucks up to the likes of Flash. In this cartoon, however, he appears not to be part of the popular crowd, but rather an average student, and he doesn’t really suck up to Flash or any of the other popular kids.In the comics, he was one of Peter Parker's childhood friends before he distanced himself from Peter after joining the popular crowd at hih school and becoming one of his bullies, wheras in this cartoon, it appears that he’s on neutral terms with Peter as he doesn’t know him that well, and is always friendly and polite when talking to him. In the comics, he's part of Flash Thompson’s gang and a popular student who sucks up to the likes of Flash. In this cartoon, however, he appears not to be part of the popular crowd, but rather an average student, and he doesn’t really suck up to Flash or any of the other popular kids. In the comics, he was one of Peter Parker's childhood friends before he distanced himself from Peter after joining the popular crowd at hih school and becoming one of his bullies, wheras in this cartoon, it appears that he’s on neutral terms with Peter as he doesn’t know him that well, and is always friendly and polite when talking to him.

characters.name: Joseph "Robbie" Robertson
characters.description: Editor-in-chief of theDaily Bugleand Randy Robertson's father. Benevolent Boss: Not that Jamesonisn'ta decent boss (if veryabrasive), but Robbie is at the very least much more cordial and reasonable than Jonah. Demoted to Extra: His role here is a lot more minimal compared to the Robbie Robertson of the comics, and his relation to his Randy only comes up once. Foil: Par for the course he is pretty much Jonah's polar opposite in every way — a patient and professionalReasonable Authority Figurewho looks at Spider-Man objectively in contrast to a loudmouthed and cantankerousMean Bosswho detests the web-head.

characters.name: Betty Brant
characters.description: J. Jonah Jameson's secretary at theDaily Bugle. Adaptational Relationship Overhaul: In the comics, she was Peter's first properLove Interest, dating him in high school. Here, while Peter does briefly show interest in her, it never goes anywhere due to the age gap and is treated as a joke. Age Lift: In the comics, she and Peter are the same age. Here, much like in the Ultimate comics, Betty's at least college age while he's still in high school. Decomposite Character: Liz Allan takes her role as Peter's first legitimate girlfriend, as well as her conflict of having a brother in debt to Blackie Gaxton. Demoted to Extra: Betty in the comics was Peter's firstLove Interestduring his high school years and was a well-developed character. Here, because a lot of her mainstream counterpart's traits aregiven to Lizandshe has undergone anAge Liftto make her position as a secretary morerealistic, she's anOut of Focusrecurring side character for most of the show's run.

characters.name: Frederick Foswell
characters.description: A reporter for theDaily Buglespecializing in organized crime. Adaptational Heroism: In the comics, Foswell was secretly The Big Man, a crime lord and early member of Peter'sRogues Gallery. Here, he is merely theIntrepid Reporterhe presents himself as, and specializes in targeting organized crime families. Badass in a Nice Suit: Fosswell is a braveIntrepid Reporterwho wears good suits except while undercover. Deadpan Snarker: He has a strong sardonic streak. At one point, he makes flowery comments about what a great hero his boss's son is while sporting a bemused expression. Decomposite Character: In the comics, he was The Big Man, while here,Tombstoneis.

characters.name: Ned Lee
characters.description: A young Daily Bugle reporter who wants to learn Spider-Man's identity. Adaptational Dye-Job: His hair goes from blonde to black. Adaptational Name Change: His last name goes from Leeds to Lee, going with hisRace Lift. Adaptational Relationship Overhaul: In the comics, he and Peter frequently headbutted over their mutual interest in Betty Brant, and even after Peter moved on, there was still a fair bit of tension between them. None of this is carried over to the show, where they barely interact. Butt-Monkey: He gets little respect from Jameson, his efforts to expose Spider-Man go nowhere, and his attempt to ask Betty on a date during hisA Day in the Limelightepisode get interrupted. He does get the occasionalThrow the Dog a Bonemoment, though.

characters.name: JeanDeWolff
characters.description: JeanDeWolffis a police officer for the New York City Police Department partnered with Stan Carter. Unlike Captain Stacy and Carter, she does not consider Spider-Man as much help as most of the criminals he captures wind up being released. Adaptational Early Appearance: Much like inUltimate Spider-Man (2000), this version of Jean is a part of Peter's life in high school instead of after college. Adaptational Job Change: This version is a beat cop, not a captain. Expy: Could be one ofEliza Maza, as she's a female cop of Native American heritage. Race Lift: She is white in the comics, but is Native-American in this adaptation.

characters.name: Stan Carter
characters.description: Stan Carter is a New York City police officer partnered with JeanDeWolff. He has a short temper and has shown an appreciation of Spider-Man's vigilantism. Adaptational Early Appearance: Similar to JeanDeWolff, Stan is a part of Peter's high school life instead of college. Adaptational Heroism: He never becomes the Sin-Eater in this continuity, though it's given aMythology Gagthrough his assertion that Spider-Man doesn't "far enough" with criminals. Adaptational Job Change: This version is a beat cop, not a sergeant. Expy: As his partner is Eliza fromGargoyles, he's basically Matt Bluestone.

characters.name: Curt Connors / The Lizard
characters.description: Dr. Curtis Connors is a brilliant biologist. He accidentally transformed himself into the Lizard when he created a formula to re-grow his missing arm. Adaptational Heroism: While most versions of Curt Connors remain as the Lizard after the initial transformation, this Connors has his Lizard persona permanently eradicated after its debut and he remains a heroic ally of Peter for the rest of the series. Adaptational Nonsapience: In the comics and other animated incarnations, Connors' Lizard persona still had his intelligence even after he was mutated. Here, this version of the Lizard is a completely mindless, feral animal who doesn't even speak. Adaptation Origin Connection:This version of Curt is responsible for the creation of the spider that bit Peter and by extension, his superpowers. In the comics, the spider was enhanced by radiation in a lab demonstration completely unrelated to Connors.Curt:You look familiar, [Peter]. Weren't you the kid who was bitten-?Peter:Bitten by the science bug.His experiments with genetically-enhanced electric eels also give him a role in the creation of Electro in this continuity, rather than Max gaining his powers in a random power line accident. Furthermore, his transformation into the Lizard is a direct result of the serum being electrified by an angry Max. This version of Curt is responsible for the creation of the spider that bit Peter and by extension, his superpowers. In the comics, the spider was enhanced by radiation in a lab demonstration completely unrelated to Connors.Curt:You look familiar, [Peter]. Weren't you the kid who was bitten-?Peter:Bitten by the science bug.

characters.name: Martha Connors
characters.description: Martha Connors is Dr. Curt Connors' wife and fellow scientist. Adaptational Intelligence: Overlaps withAdaptational Job Change, but Martha is usually depicted as a normal woman of fairly average intelligence who doesn't share her husband's profession and relies entirely on Spider-Man's help to cure Curt whenever he transforms. Here, she is every bit a scientist as he is and is responsible for creating the gene cleanser that reverts him back. Happily Married: To Curt Connors, obviously. Pair the Smart Ones: In this version, she is, like her husband, a scientist. Reasonable Authority Figure: She only fires Peter from Dr. Connors' lab because, from her perspective he betrayed their trust by abandoning the effort to cure Curt in favor of getting pictures for the Bugle. She is even convinced to rehire him albeit with some reluctance, provided he doesn't let her down again.

characters.name: Debra Whitman
characters.description: Eddie's replacement at Dr. Connors' Lab after he goes missing. Adaptational Early Appearance: This version of Debra meets Peter in high school instead of as a grad student. Adaptation Personality Change: Instead of being emotionally fragile and timid, she's rather icy towards Peter when he addresses her as "Deb". Age Lift: She's older than Peter instead of around the same age. Race Lift: She'sAmbiguously Browninstead of the usual white.

characters.name: Aaron Warren
characters.description: Peter's science professor at Midtown High. Adaptation Name Change: In the comics, his name isRaymondWarren. Here, it's Aaron. Deadpan Snarker: Not immune to this. When Liz suggests that Flash tutor her over Peter, he responds accordingly:Professor Warren:I'm not sure you understand. We want your grade to goup. Foil: He's absolutelynothinglike his brother. While Aaron is an honestReasonable Authority Figurewho passes on his intellect to others through his job as a teacher, Miles is a sleazyManipulative Bastardwho gleefully screws over other people for his own benefit. Reasonable Authority Figure: He is a professional, intelligent science teacher who acknowledges Peter as the best and brightest in his class, and even provides him opportunities at the Connors' laboratory.

characters.name: Emily Osborn
characters.description: Emily Osborn is Norman Osborn's wife and Harry Osborn's mother. Adaptational Jerkass:  Emily Osborn in the comics was described as a kind and loving woman who was a caring wife to Norman Osborn, with the implication that she would've been a great mother to her son Harry Osborn had she not died from a disease when Harry was one year old. While her death was late retconned with the reveal that she went under a new identity because she was afraid of her husband, it's still clear that she loves her son and regrets not taking him with her. This version of Emily Osborn seems to be a cold, uncaring woman who doesn't even interact with her husband and son at all and doesn't appear to be particularly close to either of them, having no reaction when Harry joins the football team and not even attending his school play (and to boot lacking any excuse unlike Norman, who could at least attest to being busy with work). Adaptation Relationship OverhaulPlayed With. In the comics, Emily was described as a caring wife to Norman, who was very much in love with her and was devastated by her death, with the implication that had she lived, he would've been a better man and a better father to their son. That said, later retcons revealed that she was actually terrified of him and simply faked her death to escape his grasp. Here, she stays in his life long after Harry's birth and the two have a cold, indifferent relationship with no sign of fear or outward affection on her part — though shedoesattend his funeral when heseemingly dies.Emily in the comics was a loving, caring mother to Harry before her death, and even with the aforementioned retcon, she explicitly regrets not taking him with her. Emily in this show, by contrast, is ridiculously cold and neglectful to Harry to the extent that the two don't have asingleconversation with each other in both seasons, aside from her buying him a car offscreen. Played With. In the comics, Emily was described as a caring wife to Norman, who was very m

characters.name: Dr. Nicolas Bromwell
characters.description: Dr. Bromwell is a doctor at the New York City Emergency Hospital and a good friend of May Parker. Race Lift:His comic book counterpartwas white, but he's African-American in this adaptation.

characters.name: Calypso
characters.description: Kraven's lover who accompanies him to New York. Adaptational Wimp: Calypso became a supervillain and recurring partner of Kraven in the comics. Here, she seems to just be his non-powered lover. Beast and Beauty: Is this with Kraven after his transformation, not that she minds.Calypso:The eyes suit you, my love. Locked Out of the Loop: If Kraven's reaction at the end of his debut episode are any indicator he hadn't told her about him allowing Warren to mutate him. Maybe Magic, Maybe Mundane: Calypso in the comics usedHollywood Voodoo, it's unconfirmed if that's the case here but there is something about her. When she appeared in New York drums were playing. After Spidey defeats Kraven and webs him up he's distracted by these same drums, when he looks back the hunter is gone. He looked away for two seconds at most.

characters.name: Dr. Kafka
characters.description: The founder of and a therapist at Ravencroft Institute. She treats (or attempts to treat) insane super-criminals. Heroic Bystander: She snaps at Kraven not to touch Dr. Octavius when he advances on the latter and Otto begs to be left alone. Horrible Judge of Character: Which she really shouldn't be, considering her profession. In "Group Therapy", she deems Electro mentally stable again and arranges to have him released. The literal second she turns her back on him, he contacts Doc Ock and slips back into criminal behavior again.She also completely buys Doc Ock's innocent persona, unintentionally providing him with an alibi and allowing him to act behind the scenes as the Master Planner. No Good Deed Goes Unpunished: She genuinely tries to help her patients but they rarely, if ever, show, appreciation for her efforts. She gets Electro discharged from the Institute, only for him to use his newfound freedom to break Doc Ock, Vulture, Sandman, Rhino and the Enforcers out of prison. The next time they're seen together, Electro, whom she treated with nothing but respect and kindness while he was under her care, even outright attacks her during his escape because he was pissed she addressed him as Max. The Shrink: A mix of Well-Meaning, But Ineffective and Awesome. Her patients are super-criminals whom she treats with the same dignity and respect as one would a regular civilian and she actively supports those who she believes are ready to be re-integrated into society. Unfortunately, most of her patients aren't the least bit interested in changing their ways and often take advantage of her trusting nature for their own benefit.

characters.name: Donald Menken
characters.description: Norman Osborn's assistant and right-hand man atOsCorp. Ambiguously Evil: His presence at thecrime lord auctionselling the specs to produce an army of Rhino-themed mercenaries indicates him to be fairly shady, but he otherwise is not shown to be overtly villainous or antagonistic. Ambiguous Situation:It is unclear if he knows Norman is the Green Goblin or not, as there is evidence pointing to both.On the one hand, it's highly suspicious that Donald was the only one besides the Osborns to know about Globulin Green, and him being at the crime lord auction shows that he has no problem with engaging in illegal activity. He's also suspiciously calm when Spider-Man breaks into his apartment and accuses him of being the Goblin to his face, whichcouldmean Donald was in on the ruse.On the other hand, however, when the unmasked Norman explains how he set up Spider-Man for a fall, he never mentionsDonaldbeing aware of his secret, and there's no evidence that Donald found out without Norman's knowledge. Also, Donalddoesseem genuinely surprised and confused when the Goblin ambushes and attacks the vigilante in his apartment. On the one hand, it's highly suspicious that Donald was the only one besides the Osborns to know about Globulin Green, and him being at the crime lord auction shows that he has no problem with engaging in illegal activity. He's also suspiciously calm when Spider-Man breaks into his apartment and accuses him of being the Goblin to his face, whichcouldmean Donald was in on the ruse. On the other hand, however, when the unmasked Norman explains how he set up Spider-Man for a fall, he never mentionsDonaldbeing aware of his secret, and there's no evidence that Donald found out without Norman's knowledge. Also, Donalddoesseem genuinely surprised and confused when the Goblin ambushes and attacks the vigilante in his apartment.

characters.name: Crusher Hogan
characters.description: A show wrestler who Peter faced early in his career after first gaining his powers. Composite Character: While he's Crusher Hogan, his leotard and facing off against Peter in a cage match takes inspiration from his film counterpart,BonesawMcGraw. Heel: Naturally, being a hammy show-wrestler. Pet the Dog: He promises to make his beatdown of Spider-Man quick because by his own admission, "[he doesn't] like picking on little guys". Of course, this is before Peter uses his powers to beat Crusher with little effort, but it's the thought that counts. Truer to the Text: In thefirst Sam Raimi film, the wrestler Peter fought underwent a major case ofAdaptation Name Changefrom the original comics, going by "BonesawMcGraw". Here, he is Crusher Hogan again like his original counterpart.

characters.name: Sullivan Edwards
characters.description: A sleazy wrestling promoter and announcer. Ambiguously Brown: He has noticeably darker skin, but his ethnicity isn't specified. It should be noted that his voice actor is of Italian descent. Jerkass Has a Point: For what it's worth, hedidindicate to Peter beforehand that there would be caveats to getting paid for beating Crusher. Being a wrestling promoter, it at least makes some sense that he would want a new talent such as Spider-Man to sign on. Small Role, Big Impact: Had he not snubbed Peter of his money for refusing to sign the management contract, Peter wouldn't have felt compelled to spite him by lettingWalter Hardyescape with his money, an action that directly resulted in Ben's death.

characters.name: Billy Connors
characters.description: Curt and Martha Connors' son. A Day in the Limelight: Downplayed. The episode isn't entirely about him, but "Natural Selection" is his only major speaking role. Intergenerational Friendship: He is on good terms with Eddie, Peter, and Gwen despite them all being young adults while he is a child. "I Know You're in There Somewhere" Fight: Sadly averted; heattemptsthis with his father during the latter's rampage as The Lizard, but he proves far too feral and animalistic for it to work.

characters.name: Morris Bench
characters.description: An explosives expert doing a demolition job for Norman. Aborted Arc: There were plans to make him into Hydro-Man like in the comics, but the cancellation of the show means Bench is left as just anInnocent Bystanderfor Spider-Man to rescue from being collateral damage when Dr. Octopus tries to kill Norman for a second time. Genius Bruiser: He is noticeably huskier than Osborn or Donald and is skilled at setting up sophisticated wireless explosives. Not So Stoic: He is polite but reserved and focused on his work while meeting Peter, only to freak out when the explosives being sabotaged makes it look like he is going to die.

characters.name: The Pumpkin Heads
characters.description: Green Goblin's rarely seenMooks. Faceless Mooks: They wear pumpkin masks over their heads at all times except for when Green Goblin hired the original ones. No Name Given: None of the individual members get names (although three are seen unmasked and get some dialogue) and even the group as a whole is never referred to by name onscreen, with the Pumpkin Head name coming from other sources. Not-So-Harmless Villain: They are mostly mistreated petty crooks who are easy to defeat, but one of them hides from Spider-Man during a fight and escapes with a truck of stolen weapons. Then, once the whole gang is using those weapons (liked armed gliders and rocket launchers), they nearly kill Spider-Man a few times. Two Guys and a Girl: The original Pumpkin Heads are two men and a women who work as smash and grab thieves and seem to live together.

characters.name: L. Thompson Lincoln / Tombstone
characters.description: Also known as Tombstone, L. Thompson Lincoln is a notorious, powerful crime lord and undisputed top dog of New York's criminal underworld — at first. As the series progresses, he finds himself facing heavy opposition from Spider-Man and competition from other mobsters who intend to move in on his turf. Adaptational Badass: While the Tombstone of the comics has worked for organized crime families, he was basically a thug and hired muscle. This version is basically the show's stand-in forThe Kingpinand hence is the head of an expansive criminal organization. Adaptational Early Appearance: Here, he's active while Peter is in high school instead of after college. Adaptational Intelligence: In the comics, Tombstone was merely a thug who never finished high school. This Tombstone is the head of a major crime organization who also poses as a legitimate businessman with business savvy, manipulative skills, andpragmatismto go with it. Adapted Out: His history with Robbie Robertson isn't present here, likely since the latter's significance ismuch lessercompared to the comics.

characters.name: Hammerhead
characters.description: Hammerhead is a criminal famous for his steel-plated skull. He worked for Tombstone before moving out on his own. Adaptational Early Appearance: Much like inUltimate Spider-Man (2000), he and Peter first butt heads while the latter's in high school instead of college. Badass in a Nice Suit: He's never seen wearing anything other than a pinstriped suit, in keeping with his 20s gangster aesthetic. Big Bad Wannabe: He attempts to betray Tombstone in the second seasonbut is ultimately only anUnwitting Pawnfor the Green Goblin's own rise to power, as his successes largely stem from piggybacking off schemes the Goblin has already put into motion. Distressed Dude: In "The Uncertainty Principle", he is kidnapped by the Green Goblin and used as a bait to trap Spider-Man and Tombstone. And he's not happy about it:Hammerhead:This is so embarrassing...

characters.name: Hammerhead's Chauffeur
characters.description: A mysterious woman who assists Hammerhead in his criminal activities. Bodyguarding a Badass: She is a gun-tottingBadass Driver, but the man she guards is a metahuman whom few can defeat. Canon Foreigner: Almost uniquely among the recurring and notable guest characters in the show, she seems to be a completely original creation with no apparent counterpart in the comics. Dark Action Girl: She is aBadass Driverwho is willing to shoot at well-armed supervillains and knows how to use a spike strip to disable a vehicle. Satellite Character: She spends all of her screen time doing whatever Hammerhead wants or needs of her, is unnamed, has no dialogue, and gets little characterization. The creator has stated that she would have become more important later on, however.

characters.name: In General
characters.description: Venom is the result of a bond between Eddie Brock and the alien symbiote previously worn by Spider-Man. Eddie's hatred of Peter Parker combined with the symbiote's betrayal by Spider-Man make them one of the greatest foes for the web-slinger alongside Doctor Octopus and Green Goblin. Adaptational Early Appearance: Much like inUltimate Spider-Man (2000), he's a part of Peter's high school life instead of after college. Adaptational Villainy: This is one of the most evil versions of Venom yet, beating even the Raimi Films one. He does multiple vile things to spite Peter that his comic book counterpart wouldn't do, trying to murder Gwen Stacy, setting a building full of innocents aflame, and gaslighting Colonel Jupiter to insanity. Animal-Themed Superbeing: Venom is a spider-based villain, justified in that the symbiote's first and favorite host was Spider-Man. Arch-Enemy: The symbiote, especially with Eddie as its host, shares this status alongside the Green Goblin. While Green Goblin's actions are greater in scope (being responsible for a large portion of Spidey's Rogues Gallery), Venom is a far more personal enemy to the web-swinger by putting his loved ones in danger.

characters.name: "Montana" / Shocker
characters.description: The leader of the Enforcers, Montana is a professional, seasoned mercenary with a distinct Southern drawl. He becomes The Shocker after acquiring a specialized suit and gauntlets, and briefly serves as a member of the Sinister Six. Adaptational Badass: As a natural result of being aComposite Character, Montana is lifted from a somewhat obscure, mundane albeit distinctBadass Normalhitman to a notable and — despite a reputation otherwise — dangerous member of Peter'sRogues Gallery. Affably Evil: Downplayed. While he's an unapologeticProfessional Killer, and thus isn't the friendliest person out there, he can be genuinely cordial at times and is consistently shown to be respectful towards his teammates, be it in the Sinister Six (aside from a brief disagreement) or The Enforcers. He's also rather open about the fact that his conflict with Spider-Manisn't personal, not that it makes him reluctant to kill him. As Lethal as It Needs to Be:He can use the airblasts to punch through steel and tunnel through rock, yet they only seem to have a concussive effect on living targets.He also only uses his lasso to subdue Spider-Man in "Final Curtain", when the most effective and lethal option would be to try choking the life out of him with it. He can use the airblasts to punch through steel and tunnel through rock, yet they only seem to have a concussive effect on living targets.

characters.name: "Fancy Dan" / Ricochet
characters.description: Fancy Dan is the dexterous hand-to-hand fighter of the Enforcers. He later acquires technology to become Ricochet. Adaptational Villainy: Due to his nature as aComposite Character, he becomes an antagonistic version of the heroic Ricochet identity of the comics. Bouncing Battler: His suit lets him become aHyper-Destructive Bouncing Ball. Clothes Make the Superman: His suit is what grants him his abilities. Composite Character: Fancy Dan and Ricochet are two different characters in the comics.

characters.name: "Ox"
characters.description: Ox is the muscle of the Enforcers. He later acquires a suit that enhances his strength to superhuman levels. The Brute: He's the Enforcers' muscle. Clothes Make the Superman: As with Ricochet and Shocker, he wears a suit that grants him superhuman abilities. Fourth-Wall Observer: He somehow knows the theme song of the show.He finds it catchy. Meaningful Rename:Averted. He insists on still going by "Ox" after donning his new suit.

characters.name: Silvio "Silvermane" Manfredi
characters.description: Also known as Silvermane, Silvio Manfredi is an infamous crime boss who once ruled the criminal underworld until he was exposed and arrested. In Season 2, he is released from prison and intends to reclaim his position as the top dog of New York organized crime. Achilles' Heel: If you succeed in damaging his suit's hydraulics, it stops functioning, leaving him helpless. Adaptational Early Appearance: He and Peter first butt heads while the latter's in high school instead of college. Adaptational Nationality: In the comics he's Italian, while here he seems to be American. Arc Villain: Of the Criminology Arc. While apart of aBig Bad Ensemblewith Tombstone and Doctor Octopus, his release from prison is what kicks off theMob Warthat serves as the central conflict of the story arc.

characters.name: Sable Manfredi / Silver Sable
characters.description: Sable Manfredi, also known as Silver Sable, is the daughter of the criminal Silvermane. Abnormal Ammo: Her gun fires what can only be described as giant staples. Adaptational Early Appearance: Much like inUltimate Spider-Man (2000), she and Spider-Man first meet while Peter's in high school instead of after college. Adaptational Job Change: In the comics, Silver Sable is a mercenary and the owner of a PMC organization known as Sable International. Her show counterpart is amob enforcer and assassinunder the employ of her father, Silvermane. Adaptational Nationality: In the comics, she's the from the fictional eastern European country of Symkaria. Here, she is American.

characters.name: Roderick Kingsley
characters.description: Aborted Arc: It's been confirmed that he was slated to become Hobgoblin in Season 3, just as in the comics. Adaptational Early Appearance: He already making moves in the underworld while Peter is in high school instead of after college. Age Lift: Judging by his white hair, Kingsley is a couple of decades older than he was in his earlier comics appearances. Corrupt Corporate Executive: Shows up at an auction alongside New York's biggest crime lords, despite publicly just being a perfume company owner. Mood-Swinger: He's calm and smug at the auction, but when we see him next, he's jittery and paranoid. However, given what we know of him in the comics, it's heavily implied thatit wasn't him picking up the suit, but his twin brother Daniel, who he does use as a body double. This is helped by the fact he has to ditch his jacket during the fight at the pickup location and then we next see Kingsley, he's still wearing it and is as calm and smug as he was at the auction.

characters.name: Blackie Gaxton
characters.description: A bookkeeper and the manager of Shocker's bar,The Big Sky Billiard Room. Evil Brit: He has a British accent, and he becomes a minion for the Green Goblin. Fantastically Indifferent: Zigzagged. Both Spidey and Green Goblin have burst into the bar he runs, trashed the place, and beat up his clientele, and he never even stood up, though he did look scared when a pissed-off Molten Man was about to attack him. Karma Houdini Warranty: At the end of "Subtext", The Big Sky is burned down. Given it's somewhat his own fault you don't feel too bad for him.Gaxton:Montana's not gonna be happy. Kick the Dog: Turns Mark, who is still in high school, over to Green Goblin as a lab rat to make him pay off the debt he owes him.

characters.name: Otto Octavius / Doctor Octopus
characters.description: Otto Octavius was a brilliant scientist and inventor before an accident bonded him to four mechanical tentacles driving him to extreme criminal activities. Taking the name Doctor Octopus, Doc Ock for short, he became one of Spider-Man's most formidable opponents, founded the Sinister Six, and became a central player in the city's criminal underworld. Adaptational Achilles' Heel: Most versions of Doc Ock animate their tentacles through sheer force of will. This version requires a power source to operate his. His first battle with Spidey (which he is close to winning) is cut short when he realizes his current battery is running low on power, and several of his later defeats revolve around the webslinger removing his other batteries. Adaptation Dye-Job: Traditionally, Doc Ock's tentacles are drawn as a metallic silver. Here, they are black with white markings. Adaptation Personality Change: The mainstream version of Otto was an arrogant jerk before his transformation. In the show, he is more of an ethical and meekExtreme Doormatconstantly mistreated by Norman Osborn and his motivation for villainy is to prove that he is no longer weak. Affably Evil: Provided he isn't angered, he's generally quite polite and dignified. He allows Aunt May to pass and behaves like a perfect gentleman before attacking Spider-Man.

characters.name: Flint Marko / Sandman
characters.description: Flint Marko was a petty criminal until an accident turned him into a being comprised of and able to control sand, known as Sandman. Adaptational Early Appearance: Marko appeared in the ninth issue in the comics, but shows up in the first episode before becoming Sandman in the fifth episode. Adaptational Name Change: In the comics, Sandman's real name is William Baker, with "Flint Marko" only used as an alias. As was the case withUltimate Spider-Man (2000)and theSpider-Man Trilogy, the latter is his real name here. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: He and O'Hirn act as a duo before gaining superpowers. The two never met before in the comics until after gaining their powers. Anti-Villain: Deep down, Marko isn't a terrible person. He's mostly motivated by money and getting back at Spider-Man for constantly humiliating him when he was a petty thug. "First Steps" shows his more human side, where he builds a huge sandcastle for a little girl, and later stops an oil tanker explosion.

characters.name: Alex O'Hirn / The Rhino
characters.description: Alex O'Hirn is a former small time crook who was turned into the powerhouse known as the Rhino. Achilles' Heel: His suit is such a complete seal that his body can't perspire. His face does the sweating for his entire body, which isn't a problem in normal conditions, but get him in a hot steamy area... Adaptational Badass: In the comics, Rhino's a big dumb brute Spidey beats on a regular basis. Here, he is still a dumb brute but an unstoppable force of pure destruction that Spidey can only defeat through cleverly exploiting his one real weakness, and as seen in "Accomplices", can occasionally pull one over the web-slinger with some effort. Adaptational Early Appearance: O'Hirn appeared in issue #49 in the comics, but shows up in the first episode before becoming Rhino in the sixth episode. Adaptational Name Change: In the comics, The Rhino's real name was Aleksei Sytsevich, with Alex O'Hirn simply being an alias. Here like his Ultimate counterpart the latter is his actual name.

characters.name: Max Dillon / Electro
characters.description: Electro, also known as Maxwell Dillon, is a former electrician who fell victim of a lab accident that turned him into an electricity-based supervillain and member of the Sinister Six. Adaptational Attractiveness: While he was adecent-looking guyin the comics, Max Dillonwasn't quite the youthfulPretty Boyseen in the series. Before his accidental transformation, this version of Max is portrayed as a fit,youngercoworker of Dr. Curt Connors, a sharp contrast to the middle-aged electrician with a receding hairline often found in the original source material. Adaptational Early Appearance: Electro appeared in issue 9 of the comics, but appears in the second episode. Adaptational Sympathy: Electro in the comics is little more than a violent thug who willingly became a super-criminal. In the series, he is more of aTragic Villainwho initially only wanted a cure until several encounters with Spider-Man and Doctor Octopus' grooming caused him to suffer aSanity Slippage. Adaptation Origin Connection: In the comics, Max just worked as a regular electrician with no connection towards any other characters prior to becoming Electro. In the show, Max got his powers in Dr. Connors' lab. This also means he has a connection with Peter/Spider-Man before becoming Electro, as in the comics, Spidey never knew about Electro's identity.

characters.name: Adrian Toomes / The Vulture
characters.description: Adrian Toomes was an elderly aerodynamics engineer who used his designs to become the supervillain Vulture after Norman Osborn fired him. Appropriated Appellation:Parodied. He takes the name "Vulture" based on what Norman referred to him as… though Normanactuallycalled him a buzzard. Astonishingly Appropriate Appearance: Osborn didn't call him a buzzard for nothing. His long nose and slotted pupils make him look almost exactly like his namesake. Badass Bookworm: Makes powered armor and goes toe to toe with Spidey. Bald of Evil: Toomes is a bald old man, but nevertheless a criminal.

characters.name: Sergei Kravinoff / Kraven The Hunter
characters.description: Kraven the Hunter is a highly skilled big-game hunter capable of taking down his quarries with his bare hands who sets out to vanquish Spider-Man and was transformed into a cat-like creature. Adaptational Wimp: Zigzagged withAdaptational Badass. Traditionally, Kraven is able to hold his own against Spider-Man fairly easily. Here, he puts up a decent fight but is ultimately humiliated, and is only able to become a genuine threat by transforming himself into a lion-human hybrid with superhuman abilities. All Your Powers Combined: Kraven specifically asks for his DNA getting combined with African big cats, granting him the speed of acheetah, the agility of a leopard and the strength of a lion. Arrogant Kung-Fu Guy: He has shades of this along withEgomaniac Hunter(see below). The fact that he gave Spider-Man a decent fight as a normal human isn't enough for him since he was humiliated. He makes defeating Spider-Man and proving himself as a hunter/fighter as more important than anything else, even losing his humanity to better fight Spider-Man (and to stubbornly press forward when Spider-Manstillbeats him). Badass Normal: Initially, but he doesn't remain so past his first encounter with Spider-Man. Spidey himself notes that Kraven is arguably second to none when it comes to natural human strength, but this does him little good against a guy withsuperstrength.

characters.name: Quentin Beck / Mysterio
characters.description: Quentin Beck was a film special effects expert. He eventually became a supervillain under the name Mysterio where he joined the Sinister Six. Actually a Doombot: During the first time Spidey catches him, the Mysterio that was captures turned out to be a robot double. The second time, Spidey is smart enough to pinch Beck to make sure he caught the real one — and then it later turns out that this Beck wasalsoa robot double. Adorable Evil Minions: The gargoyle-like robots he uses, which would also qualify asThe Imp. Jameson amusingly lampshades this, remarking that someone should give themtheir own show. Affably Evil: He can come off as very likable and snarky at times despite being a villainous thief. Badass Cape: The eye-shaped clasps can even shoot lasers.

characters.name: Phineas Mason / Tinkerer
characters.description: Phineas Mason, also known as Tinkerer, is a genius inventor who has worked with several major supercriminals who fought against Spider-Man. The Dragon: He serves this role to the Master Planner for a time, acting as his main technical support. Evil Genius: He's an inventor who enjoys making tech for the likes of Chameleon and Doctor Octopus. Gadgeteer Genius: Just like his comic book counterpart, he cobbles most of his inventions together from scraps and junk, he has a fairly low overhead and thus is a go-to guy for the budget conscious super-villain. Non-Action Guy: As kindly pointed out by Mysterio: "Strictly technical support. Trust me, he isuselessin a fight."

characters.name: Eddie Brock
characters.description: One of Peter and Gwen's closest friends and current assistant to Doctor Connors, a series of unfortunate events that send Eddie's life tumbling down the drain drive him to violent extremes when he comes into possession of the symbiote. Aborted Arc: Eddie's role in Season 2 ended with Peter using the gene cleanser to separate the Venom symbiote from him. Eddie is then wheeled out on a stretcher screaming that Peter is Spider-Man, he is Venom, and that when the symbiote returns they'll destroy their enemy once and for all. Given Cletus Kasady's cameo appearance, had the show continued, Eddie would have ended up in Ravencroft and been busted out by the Venom symbiote, leading to Kasady becoming Carnage. Adaptational Friendship: Much like his Ultimate counterpart, he is a childhood friend of Peter's before his descent into villainy. He's also a friend of Gwen Stacy here, which neither his classic counterpart (who was introduced well after she died and never met her) or his Ultimate counterpart (who that universe's Gwen almost immediately pegged as a creep) were. Adaptational Intelligence: Due to being a lab assistant like his Ultimate counterpart, Eddie is shown to be smarter than his mainstream version. This is further shown with being able to build his own web shooter as part of hisParanoia Gambit. Adaptational Job Change: Following the footsteps of his Ultimate self, Eddie's initially a lab assistant rather than a journalist.

characters.name: The Symbiote
characters.description: A mysterious alien creature unintentionally brought to Earth after a routine space mission, the symbiote eventually escapes containment and bonds to Spider-Man, granting him even more incredible powers at just as dangerous a cost. 2D Visuals, 3D Effects: The symbiote's first appearance. It's not the usual 3D model example, but is instead a black blob whose shine doesn't at all conform to the curve of the space shuttle's hull. It's like an awkward piece of clipart. Adaptational Badass: Due to the symbiote explicitly drawing power from the negative emotions of its hosts here, it takes a lot more than Peter punching a church bell like previous incarnations to force it off him, requiring an entireBattle in the Center of the Mind. Adaptational Villainy: TakingTruer to the Textinto account, Eddie and the symbiote have switched roles in terms of who turned whom to villainy. The symbiote was originally a passive entity that got driven insane by Eddie's hatred for Spider-Man, while here, it's an irrefutably malevolent and vengeful creature that feeds off the anger and hate of its hosts, not to mention how it mentally tortured Parker to force him into being a submissive host. Ambiguous Situation: It's left unclear justwhyit suddenly abandons Eddie Brock at the end of his final fight with Peter, asWord of Godstated that, despite the scene framing it as such, it had nothing to do with Eddie being force-fed the gene cleanser.

characters.name: Felicia Hardy / Black Cat
characters.description: Black Cat is the code name of Felicia Hardy. She is a thief and daughter of Walter Hardy. Her path often crosses with Spider-Man. Adaptational Modesty: As with most adaptations, Black Cat's outfit here doesn't show any cleavage, but is still very form-fitting. Age-Gap Romance: Downplayed, as the two aren't anOfficial Couple, but she is evidently interested in Spider-Man while being three years older than him (she's confirmed to be nineteen, while Peter is sixteen). Audible Sharpness: Her claws make a noticeable "shink" sound whenever she sharpens them. Bad Is Good and Good Is Bad: Apparently, if a "hero" like Spider-Man and his "stupid conscience" meansher father will choose to stay in prison, then she'd rather stick with her life of crime and stop going easy on him.

characters.name: The Chameleon
characters.description: The Chameleon is a supervillain mercenary and master of disguise. Adaptational Late Appearance: The Chameleon was Spider-Man'sStarter Villainin the comics, debuting in Issue #1. Here, he first appears in Episode 10, though is later revealed to have been active earlierdisguised as Norman Osborn— still not first supervillain Peter faces in any case. Adaptational Wimp: In most adaptations and the comics, Chameleon can almost perfectly copy the identities of other peoples andDepending on the Writeris an outright shapeshifter. His show counterpart is much more down to Earth, as while his masks are a case ofLatex Perfection, he explicitly requires very obvious gadgets to copy the likes of Spider-Man, and on two occasions misses key details about the personalities of the people he impersonates, cluing others in to the fact that he is an imposter. The Blank: A variation: He has visible eyes and a mouth, just really no other facial features. Cast as a Mask: Every one of his disguises uses the voice actor of that character.

characters.name: John Jameson / Colonel Jupiter
characters.description: John Jameson is an Air Force colonel, astronaut, and J. Jonah Jameson's son. The Ace: Just like his comic book counterpart, he's a highly experienced pilot and astronaut. At least before hisFace–Heel Turn. Anti-Villain: He made a pretty good hero, but after he mistook Venom for Spider-Man, and thought Spidey was pulling his ownFace–Heel Turn, he went out to kill him. Brought Down to Normal: Spider-Man cures his spore-induced condition, but it's possible (though unconfirmed) he would've somehow transformed intoMan-Wolfhad the series continued. Deadpan Snarker: He reacts rather well to growing twice his size and being forced to wear a containment suit.

characters.name: Miles Warren
characters.description: Professor Aaron Warren's brother and a renowned, and highly corrupt, scientist. Adaptational Early Appearance: Much like inUltimate Spider-Man (2000), this version of Miles is a part of Peter's life in high school instead of college. Badass Bookworm: He's aNon-Action Guy, sure, but when a huge burly hunter walks into his lab with a living lion and starts asking questions about Spider-Man, what does Warren do? He doesn't bat an eye, lies about giving Spidey his powers and even compliments the lion as a magnificent specimen. When Kraven demands to be enhanced as well, Warren calmly requests a hefty payment and when Kraven threatens to sic his lion on him as coercion, he just coolly points out that it's a very bad idea to threaten the person you want to tamper with your genetic code. He receives his payment. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Just look at the pic. This guy looksnothinglike a villain and acts pretty affable at the beginning. Yet, as the series goes on, it becomes quite clear he is a complete bastard. Had the show gone on, he likely would have adopted his supervillain persona, The Jackal, in a future season. Cain and Abel: It's not revealed what his relationship with his brother is like, but they're definitely nothing alike.

characters.name: Mark Allan / Molten Man
characters.description: Mark Allan is Liz Allan's big brother. He eventually becomes an unwilling test subject for Norman Osborn, thus becoming the supervillain Molten Man. Adaptational Dumbass: In the comics, Molten Man was a scientist who always learned from his defeats. In this adaptation, he only has average intelligence, is sorely lacking in common sense, and (as his gambling addiction shows) doesn't learn from his mistakes. Adaptational Name Change: In the comics, his surname was Raxton due to being Liz Allen’s stepbrother rather than her biological brother. Anti-Villain: He's less of an actively malevolent criminal and more of a troubled teenager whose gambling addiction gets him in major trouble. He doesn't even go out of his way to target Spider-Man until The Green Goblin manipulates him into doing so. Big Brother Instinct: Whatever his faults, he does care for his little sister and wishes only the best for her.
